 Knicks need Mikal Bridges ready for a familiar Cavs test
 Alexander Wilson 
 Published : November 7, 2026 
 Share on Facebook 
 Share on Twitter 
 Share on Flipboard 
 Share via Email 
 The Knicks return to Cleveland on Saturday with a familiar defensive problem: Donovan Mitchell can change a game before a defense finishes setting its help.
 Mikal Bridges should get an early opportunity to take that assignment. Josh Hart is out with right ankle soreness, CBS Sports reported , making New York’s available perimeter defenders even more important. The matchup is a regular-season meeting, not a replay of the Eastern Conference finals New York swept in May.
 Nov 4, 2026; New York, New York, USA; Chicago Bulls guard Buddy Hield (7) drives to the basket against New York Knicks guard Mikal Bridges (25) during the second quarter at Madison Square Garden. Mandatory Credit: Brad Penner-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect 
 The Knicks cannot ask Bridges to do it alone
 New York beat Cleveland in four games last postseason, Axios reported . In Game 3, Bridges scored 22 points while Mitchell had 23, according to the game report . Those numbers establish the stakes, not proof Bridges individually caused Mitchell’s performance.
 I’d start with Bridges applying pressure at the point of attack and keep help close enough to protect against drives. The important part is the second defender’s timing: send help too early and Cleveland gets clean passes; arrive too late and Mitchell has room to finish or create.

 OG Anunoby is an obvious alternative for stretches, especially if screens repeatedly force a switch. New York can also vary coverages instead of handing the same assignment to one player for the entire night.
 The Cavaliers have different personnel and the season is young, so a spring sweep is not a forecast. The Knicks should use their perimeter depth to make Mitchell work while preserving enough flexibility to adjust to James Harden and the rest of Cleveland’s offense.
